newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real closes the year down 6.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real closes the year down 6.9 pct.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.05 percent to close at 1.0391 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market Tuesday, ending the year 6.9 percent lower, dealers said.
In December the real fell 0.61 percent, they said.
The market had very low turnover Tuesday as banks were only allowed to trade until midday in the interbank market.

Shortly after the open, the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency of 1.0390 to 1.0440 per dollar through a buy/sell auction, dealers said. The previous mini-band was set on December 23 between 1.0385 and 1.0435.
The mini-band was lowered 6.9 percent this year by the Central Bank, dealers added.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating-rate market, the real fell 0.09 percent to end at 1.0450 per dollar in very thin trade.
The real fell 0.65 percent in December and dropped 6.96 percent during the year in the floating-rate market, traders said.
The illegal parallel market was closed Tuesday. The real closed there Monday at 1.120 per dollar, down 12 percent on the year.
